summary: This paper establishes four sharp quantitative laws governing the spectral Braess paradox for normalized Laplacians under subgraph additions. The authors prove universal multiplicative Weyl bounds identifying optimal budget-k saboteurs (cliques versus triangle-free graphs), an exact degeneracy immunity theorem showing that sparse graphs of bounded degeneracy are completely immune to Braess collapse regardless of size, an asymmetric single-edge law revealing a strict Cheeger-spectral rift, and regular-graph localization obstructions with a complete equipartite classification. All 15 core theorems are rigorously certified in Lean 4 with zero sorry.
strengths: Complete formal certification of all 15 core theorems in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry and zero custom axioms.
Resolves the exact worst-case spectral degradation across four distinct perturbation regimes.
Introduces the concept of degeneracy immunity, proving that d-degenerate graphs have a strict size-independent immunity floor.
Discovers the asymmetric Cheeger-spectral rift, proving that spectral gaps can drop strictly below the Cheeger conductance floor.
Provides exhaustive numerical validation across 2,500 random graphs and closed-form extremal families.
weaknesses: The analysis is restricted to edge-disjoint subgraph additions, leaving overlapping edge modifications for future work.
Certain asymptotic bounds for regular graphs rely on Alon-Boppana thresholds that could potentially be tightened for specific degree ranges.
